alK.text:
used for layer priority...
this is a work around to not add lots of other variables such as "clone type", "clone family" or whatever..

alM.text: don't forget the size of entities changes...

alO.text: don't forget the size of entities changes...

alU.text:
This is to do one type of ordering after the other and not both at the same time which causes problems...
It's also a work around because my simpler solution froze the game in scratch.

alW.text:
This is to do one type of ordering after the other and not both at the same time which causes problems...
It's also a work around because my simpler solution froze the game in scratch.

alY.text:
Unused blocks
I used to set each character manually, but this is not required anymore.

al%.text: for some reason if i don't put this block the exp amount is not reset properly by the block below?

al).text: for some reason i haven't figured out yet, i have to call "start ordering" each time i try to order by a variable instead of doing it after trying to order by multiple variables.

al+.text: The value of this variable must be set  AFTER initialization, (BEFORE that, the CLONE. layer family  variable doesn't have the proper value!!)

al/.text: The value of this variable must be set  AFTER initialization, (BEFORE that, the CLONE. layer family  variable doesn't have the proper value!!)

al;.text: The value of this variable must be set  AFTER initialization, (BEFORE that, the CLONE. layer family  variable doesn't have the proper value!!)

al?.text: It's necessary to use this function because sprite. dx dy below can change the costume then change it again to the one saved in variable, leading to stamping another costume. (this function here sets the variable to the costume you enter)

al^.text:
This is to have sharp borders
(this counters anti aliasing on the edges)

This is also so that rounded corners do not look like they are protruding from the edges

al~.text: not an angle just a holder variable here...

amj.text: the sqrt here is experimental, i can't give a justification  for it other than that it looks closer to the true color that way...

aj/.text:
Use multiple of 90° for the angle.
This is not guaranteed to work at all, test beforehand. 
If it does work, it'll give you "insane" precision though.

aj[.text: Scratch will handle limiting the size. If you divide 54000 by the size, you actually approximately get the average between the weight and height of the sprite.
